description: We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters. Ford’s Electric Vehicles, Digital and Design (EVDD) team is charged with delivering the company’s vision of a fully electric transportation future. EVDD is customer-obsessed, entrepreneurial, and data-driven and is dedicated to delivering industry-leading customer experience for electric vehicle buyers and owners. You’ll join an agile team of doers pioneering our EV future by working collaboratively, staying focused on only what matters, and delivering excellence day in and day out. Join us to make positive change by helping build a better world where every person is free to move and pursue their dreams. In this position... The global supply chain behind UEV must be as innovative as the platform itself. As Global Supply Manager, you’ll own the end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical vehicle spend. You’ll partner with engineering from concept through launch, using first-principles decision-making to deliver breakthrough outcomes. You will lead global supplier negotiations and structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without sacrificing cost leverage. You’ll also play a central role in one of the most complex challenges facing the industry today: designing a supply chain that is resilient to geopolitical risk and compliant with a rapidly evolving global trade and tariff environment. What you'll do... Own end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical spend areas across the UEV platform and follow-on advanced EV programs from sourcing strategy development through SOP, including supplier selection, contracting, and ongoing cost, quality, and delivery performance. Partner with engineering from concept through launch to align sourcing strategy with technical roadmaps, design freeze milestones, and prototype-to-production transitions. Structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without ceding cost leverage. Build first-principles should-cost models with cross-functional teams to drive a ground-up, physics-based part and system cost perspective. Use these models to set negotiation positions, evaluate quote submissions, and challenge supplier pricing line by line. Lead make-vs-buy analysis to ensure we have a best-in-class supply chain that delivers optimal value. Develop the supply base for resilience. Identify and qualify Tier 1 and Tier 2 partners across geographies; build dual-source and regional capacity strategies that address raw material scarcity, geopolitical risk, and an evolving global trade and tariff environment. Drive automation across the supply chain to deliver best-in-class supply chain efficiency. Partner with suppliers to identify opportunities for process automation and robotics. Shape the tools and processes the ADVEV supply chain runs on, including should-cost methodology, supplier and agreement management systems, and AI-enabled analytics that scale how Ford evaluates suppliers, parts, and agreements. You'll have... Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. 5+ years of experience in supply chain management or commodity management. Experience bringing creative negotiation skills and out-of-the-box strategy. Strong relationship management skills with internal and external stakeholders. Even better, you may have... Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, or related field, or MBA. Hands-on experience building and launching highly effective supply chains. Strong written and verbal communication skills. An eagerness to work cross-functionally in a dynamic environment where you are part of a high performing team. A systems approach to design and development with the desire and curiosity to strive for exceptional delivery execution and continuous improvement. Eagerness to expand into new commodity areas as the ADVEV portfolio grows. description: About ITT ITT Inc. description: What You’ll Do The Procurement Associate supports the sourcing and purchasing of materials, equipment, and services critical to pharmaceutical manufacturing and business operations. What We’re Looking For Experience • 0–3 years of procurement, purchasing, or supply chain experience in a manufacturing or cGMP-regulated environment preferred. • Experience working with ERP systems such as SYSPRO, SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms is a plus. • Prior experience coordinating with suppliers, warehouses, and cross-functional stakeholders preferred. Education • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline required. description: About Vantage Data Centers Vantage Data Centers powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands. Procurement Department The team leads these efforts from conception through commissioning, working with Sales, Operations, New Site Development, and Engineering along the way. Procurement also works closely with vendor partners to come up with a vertically integrated design, and we manage these partners to deliver the projects on schedule and budget. One thing that distinguishes Vantage is that our technical staff is given the responsibility and authority to directly drive the process. When compared to external resources, our internal team can align long-term operational sustainability with value engineering and cost metrics to deliver products aligned with corporate goals. This approach empowers each member of the team to drive high- impact decisions and even more impactful results. Position Overview This position will be based on-site at our office in Ashburn, VA in alignment with our flexible work policy (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible). Vantage is looking for a self-starter in the role of a Senior Procurement Analyst to be part of a team that manages OFCI Equipment, which is the second largest individual cost within the construction process, and to become engaged in the supply chain aspects of our Data Centers. In this role, you will be responsible for record keeping, assist in obtaining vendors submittals, maintaining product specifications, working with vendors, working with the Procurement team to ensure specifications are adhered to in accordance to our company process, monitor and managing contracts, prepare status and tracking reports for the company, support the Procurement Managers and Senior Director in their daily tasks. Regular collaboration and coordination are required with our supply chain partners and internal teams such as Engineering, Operations, Legal, as well as multiple Construction Management Teams. Travel will be necessary to various factories for factory witness testing, audits, and on-boarding of new vendors. Minimal travel to Vantage Data Center sites may also be required occasionally. Essential Job Functions The individual will be continuously working with the procurement team to provide the daily assistance needed to ensure the department meets and exceeds its goals with the company. Individual will be a self-starter and with the ability to manage and assist multiple single line diagrams, product specifications and driving OFCI Equipment submittals to closure (approval). Successful candidate will understand RFIs and RFQs for the sourcing of equipment for low voltage switchgear, medium switchgear, transformers, electrical skids, CRAH’s, chillers, generators, UPS’s and other data center equipment systems as needed. Coordinate with vendors on continuous quality improvement. Manage and track equipment status with the vendors such that all scheduled dates set by the construction schedules are met. Analyze and negotiate vendor quotes, change orders and back charges. Learn and manage the financial software to enter PO’s, review invoices, track budgets, allocate equipment from purchase to the projects. Support Procurement Managers and Finance / Accounting with invoicing issues. Drive project-level tasks and milestones assigned by the project management team. Coordinates with vendors for scheduling start-up and commissioning support services from the vendors Maintain and develop supplier relationships. Help develop and maintain record keeping and reports for the business. Continue to work and help refine the procurement processes to make sure they are complying and efficient. Work with compliance to maintain the department and vendors are within guidelines. Work with operational personnel of the Vantage buildings to ensure the proper spare parts and service programs are properly in place and assist with their database. Continue safety evaluations with vendors and project sites to make compliance is met. Senior Analyst should be able to manage the full OFCI equipment package on a VDC development project with minimal support/assistance from a Procurement Manager. Duties Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure clarity of the specifications and operational requirements. Work with finance and compliance to ensure all purchases have appropriately been costed to a project. Help coordinate the approval and release of the necessary equipment per construction schedule. Continue to investigate and work with vendors to make sure their products are best suited for Vantage. Support open and transparent communication with project teams for project delivery success. Negotiate complex requests for equipment and services from suppliers and subcontractors. Manage equipment inventory planning efforts and forecasting. Additional Duties as assigned by Management. Job Requirements Bachelor of Science in engineering, construction science, supply chain management, logistics, business administration, or related field or equivalent experience, is required. 3+ years of experience in a supply chain or construction role is required. Data Center, commercial, or industrial equipment experience is strongly preferred. Ability to learn quickly and drive things to closure. Strong business acumen with a strong commercial background. Knowledge of sourcing and procurement techniques. Travel is expected to be up to 10% but may increase over time as the business evolves. Additional Details Salary Range: $95,000-105,000 Base + Bonus (this range is based on Virginia market data and may vary in other locations) This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits. Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including your qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience and may fall outside of the range shown We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. We find joy in our work and each other, actively seeking opportunities to inject fun into what we do. Our hard and efficient work is rewarded with an above market total compensation package. Throughout the year, the advantage of being part of the Vantage team is evident with an array of benefits, recognition, training and development, and the knowledge that your contribution adds value to the company and our community. Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To: Our Buyer Sr. will ensure program requirements are appropriately prioritized and executed to meet the needs Blue Origin. Strong analytical skills, data driven with experience in establishing and tracking program metrics Create and maintain systems and processes to streamline operations. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. Conduct spend analysis, supplier evaluations, market research, and benchmarking to identify sourcing opportunities. Partner closely with Operations, Finance, Legal, and business leaders to align procurement activities with organizational goals. Lead cross-functional sourcing initiatives and facilitate stakeholder alignment throughout the procurement process. Represent Procurement in strategic projects and transformation initiatives across US and European markets. Develop and deliver training, guidance, and best practices to support procurement process adoption and compliance. Required Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, or a related field required. Experience: 5+ years of progressive procurement and strategic sourcing experience, including category management, supplier negotiations, competitive sourcing events, contract management, and stakeholder engagement. Demonstrates ownership, accountability, and a proactive approach to problem solving. Comfortable managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Effective communicator with the ability to build relationships across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and business teams. Droisys believes in diversity, inclusion, and belonging, and we are committed to fostering a diverse work environment

description: Job Summary The Procurement Manager, Major Projects will serve as the primary Procurement partner for major generation and transmission capital projects. This role works closely with Project Management, Engineering, Construction, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Contracts, and Project Controls to develop and execute an integrated procurement plan that supports project timelines, supplier capacity, material availability, and overall project delivery. The role is a senior individual contributor and requires strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to drive results across a matrixed organization without direct authority. Key Responsibilities Lead and maintain integrated procurement plans aligned with project schedules and milestones. Coordinate procurement activities across materials, equipment, services, construction, sourcing, and contracting. Strong experience with procurement, contracting, supplier management, supply markets, lead times, and delivery assurance. Proven ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives without direct authority. Strong stakeholder management, collaboration, problem-solving, and executive communication skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with utility, generation, transmission, EPC, or infrastructure capital projects. Knowledge of project controls, critical path scheduling, commissioning, and construction sequencing. Experience managing procurement risks for $100M+ capital projects. PMP, CPSM, CPSD, SCM, or similar certification. Experience working in matrixed and portfolio-based organizations.

job_title: Head of Procurement and Supply Chain (Located in the US)
description: The Head of Procurement & Supply Chain will oversee and direct all sourcing, procurement, and supply chain activities for Gilbert's compounding pharmacy network. This position plays a vital role in maintaining a consistent supply of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), compounding materials, packaging materials, and other essential supplies needed for both 503A (patient-specific compounding) and 503B (outsourcing facility) operations. Reporting to the Director of Pharmacy Development & Operations, you'll develop vendor partnerships, negotiate agreements, manage inventory systems, and ensure compliance with FDA, USP, and cGMP standards for efficient and compliant pharmacy operations. Key Responsibilities Strategic Procurement & Vendor Management Develop and implement comprehensive procurement strategies for APIs, excipients, and compounding materials that ensure quality, compliance, cost-effectiveness, and supply continuity. Establish and maintain relationships with FDA-registered API suppliers, ensuring all materials meet USP/NF standards and cGMP requirements. Negotiate contracts, pricing, and terms with suppliers while maintaining quality standards and regulatory compliance. Build redundancy in the supply chain with qualified backup vendors for critical materials. Manage vendor qualification, audits, and ongoing performance evaluation programs. API & Raw Material Sourcing Source and procure Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) from FDA-registered suppliers with appropriate Drug Master Files (DMFs). Ensure all APIs are accompanied by Certificates of Analysis (CoA) and meet compendial specifications. Manage procurement of excipients, preservatives, stabilizers, and other compounding ingredients. Coordinate with Quality Assurance on material testing and release procedures. Maintain current knowledge of API availability, market conditions, and alternative sources. 503A & 503B Compliance Materials Procure all materials necessary for regulatory compliance including environmental monitoring supplies (air sampling, surface testing), cleanroom supplies (garments, gloves, disinfectants), quality control testing materials and reference standards, sterility testing supplies and media, and endotoxin testing materials. Ensure all materials meet requirements for sterile and non-sterile compounding environments. Maintain documentation supporting regulatory inspections (FDA, state boards of pharmacy). Equipment, Packaging & Fulfillment Materials Source and procure compounding equipment (balances, hoods, autoclaves, ovens, etc.) and laboratory equipment for quality testing. Manage procurement of facility infrastructure materials for ISO-classified cleanrooms, including HVAC filters and environmental controls. Procure primary packaging (vials, syringes, bottles, jars) and secondary packaging materials (boxes, labels, shipping containers) that meet FDA and USP container closure requirements. Coordinate with fulfillment operations on shipping supplies, cold chain packaging, and temperature monitoring devices. Inventory & Supply Chain Management Develop and maintain inventory management systems for APIs, excipients, and supplies. Implement just-in-time and safety stock strategies balancing carrying costs with supply security. Monitor expiration dates and coordinate material rotation with pharmacy operations. Establish KPIs for inventory turnover, stock-out prevention, and cost management. Implement ERP or inventory management software systems. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Team Leadership Partner with Quality Assurance on vendor qualification, material specifications, and CoA review. Collaborate with Compounding Operations to forecast material needs and prevent production delays. Work with Regulatory Affairs to ensure procurement practices support licensure and inspections. Build and lead a procurement and supply chain team; develop SOPs for all procurement activities. Foster a culture of compliance, quality, and continuous improvement. Requirements 7+ years of progressive procurement and supply chain experience with at least 5 years in pharmaceutical manufacturing, compounding, or related healthcare industry. Direct experience with 503A and/or 503B compounding pharmacy operations strongly preferred. Deep understanding of FDA regulations for 503A and 503B compounding pharmacies, USP Chapters <795>, <797>, and <800> requirements, and cGMP for pharmaceutical manufacturing. Experience with API sourcing from FDA-registered suppliers and pharmaceutical raw material procurement. Knowledge of sterile compounding, aseptic processing, cleanroom operations, and pharmaceutical quality systems. Strong negotiation and contract management skills with proven vendor relationship management abilities. Proficiency with ERP systems, inventory management software, and procurement platforms. Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Pharmacy, or related field required. Preferred Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) Pharmacy Technician Certification (CPhT). Experience working within a startup or high-growth healthcare company. Existing relationships with API suppliers and pharmaceutical material vendors. What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months) Qualified vendor network established for APIs, excipients, and all critical materials with backup suppliers in place. Inventory management system implemented with zero stock-outs impacting production. All materials sourced meet FDA, USP, and cGMP requirements with full documentation supporting regulatory inspections. Cost savings achieved through strategic sourcing and contract negotiations without compromising quality. Strong collaborative partnerships established with Quality Assurance, Operations, and Regulatory Affairs teams. Standardized procurement SOPs documented and team trained on compliance requirements. Benefits Open to discussion

Initiate & Lead the supplier and product qualification process. Benchmark vendors to identify the opportunities to improve competitive pricing of each project scope.
